newsitem.title: USA: Miami police rush to possible Cunanan location.
newsitem.headline: Miami police rush to possible Cunanan location.

text.p: Police searching for Andrew Cunanan, the alleged killer of fashion designer Gianni Versace, rushed to a houseboat moored on Miami Beach on Wednesday after at least one shot was fired by a man barricaded inside.
Local television said police believed Cunanan, the subject of an intense nationwide manhunt, could be the man inside the houseboat.

Police said it was too early to link the incident, initially described as a houseboat robbery and shooting, with Cunanan. But the scale of their response -- black-garbed SWAT teams quickly surrounded the houseboat -- suggested they were treating it as more than a burglary or routine shooting incident.
FBI and state police officers also hurried to the houseboat site.
"We just have a shot fired call," said Bernie Ruder, spokesman for the Miami Beach Police Department.
He said he could not immediately confirm television reports that the houseboat's caretaker had described the man who fired from inside as dark-haired and resembling Cunanan.
"I don't have any other information on it other than that a shot was fired," he said. "We believe there is a subject barricaded inside."
Dozens of officers from across Dade County rushed to the scene and could be seen donning bullet-proof vests and other special equipment before walking around the houseboat to assess the situation.
There was no immediate indication that they had made contact with the man inside.
"We don't even know if he is inside the boat," Miami Beach police spokesman Bobby Hernandez said. He added police were certain there were no hostages on the boat.
Police cordoned off streets and the waterway surrounding the houseboat, located about 40 blocks from where Versace was killed on July 15.
Traffic backed up for miles across bridges linking Miami Beach to mainland Florida. Miami Beach, a narrow finger of land off the Miami coast, is a separate city with its own police force.

Guests at a strip of hotels inside the cordoned-off area massed on the street, craning for a view of the situation. Police attempted to shoo them back into their rooms. Local television said police were cutting off electricity to the boat.

Hernandez tried to play down speculation Cunanan, wanted for four other murders as well as that of Versace, could be the man on the boat. The intense reaction to the shooting incident was "because it's the same city where the crime occurred a week ago," he told reporters.
The incident followed possible sightings of Cunanan as far away as New Hampshire in the northeast United States, near the Canadian border.
Police in New Hampshire investigated two more sightings of a man resembling Cunanan on Wednesday, but the FBI expressed doubt a third sighting in the state was actually the alleged killer.

A woman told police early on Wednesday she saw Cunanan shopping in a K-Mart store in Claremont, New Hampshire, on Tuesday night. Another woman said she saw a man resembling the 27-year-old Cunanan in the same shopping plaza getting out of a light or white Mercedes with Florida license plates.
"We've increased our alertness that he could be in this area," Claremont Police Captain Patrick Yatsevich told Reuters. "Obviously all our detectives are involved in this."

The FBI said it had received more than 1,000 phone calls from across the country from people claiming to have spotted Cunanan. Florida police said Cunanan is a master of disguise and may be dressed as a woman.

The two unconfirmed sightings in Claremont came about eight hours after he was allegedly seen in Lebanon, New Hampshire, 20 miles (32 km) north of Claremont, police said. FBI spokesman Peter Ginieres said that based on the physical description of the man, it was probably not Cunanan.

The hunt for Cunanan also spread to Houston, where police were alerted on Wednesday that a man resembling the suspected serial killer was on board a Continental Airlines flight from Newark, New Jersey, police said.
The man was detained and questioned after Continental Flight 207 landed at Houston's Bush Intercontinental Airport, but was released after police determined he was not Cunanan.

The FBI on Tuesday said a bullet recovered from Versace's body matched the gun used in two of the four other murders of which Cunanan is suspected during a cross-country killing spree that began in April.
